subject: Using a linear regression measurement model within a logistic structural model

messages.author: 5697df62416161e2
messages.subject: Using a linear regression measurement model within a logistic structural model
parts:
Hello Everyone, 

This is a simplified version of the structural model I am attempting to run in with lavaan. The crux of my question is whether I can use what I have fit as a linear measurement model within a structural model that uses logit to predict a dichotomous variable?  Conceptually the Latents are continuous, hence my linear regression to predict them. However, when they are later used in a logistic SEM, the latents are being treated as dichotomous (?). Is there a way to use both regression techniques within one model? Alternatively, should I refit my measurement model using logit? 

#Measurement Model
Latent1 =~ Item1+Item1+Item3+Item4+Covariate
Latent2 =~ Item5+Item6+Item7+Item8+Covariate
#Outcome Model
ExcellentOutcome~Covariate+Latent1+Latent2
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ExcellentOutcome is a dichotomous variable. 
Item1-8 have 1-4 range

I first fit the measurement models for Latents 1  & 2 using linear regression (using modification indices to obtain final version). Then I used those measurement models in a structural model that predicts the dichotomous ExcellentOutcome variable using Latents 1 & 2  as predictors. 

Thank you in advance, 

Claudia Z-G

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Using a linear regression measurement model within a logistic structural model
parts: However, when they are later used in a logistic SEM, the latents are being treated as dichotomous (?).

No, lavaan only handles continuous latent variables.  In you model, your predictors are continuous latent variables.  It is the outcome (ExcellentOutcome) that is (I assume) a binary observed variable.

Is there a way to use both regression techniques within one model? Alternatively, should I refit my measurement model using logit? 

#Measurement Model
Latent1 =~ Item1+Item1+Item3+Item4+Covariate
Latent2 =~ Item5+Item6+Item7+Item8+Covariate
#Outcome Model
ExcellentOutcome~Covariate+Latent1+Latent2
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ExcellentOutcome is a dichotomous variable. 
Item1-8 have 1-4 range

The items have only 4 categories, so you should treat them as ordered when you call lavaan (see the tutorials on the lavaan web site).  By default, lavaan will use a probit link, and if you want to use a logit link, you need to use the MML estimator (see the ?lavaan help page).  Regardless of which link you use, the latent variables are continuous, not categorical.  It is only the outcomes (including indicators) that are categorical.

Terry
